subject: RFP response: Audit traceability, export formats, and time-bound retention commitments
messages:
From: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@candescent.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Darren King <darren.king@candescent.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifications on audit traceability & exportability (RFP CND-9341)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the initial RFP packet — the team at Candescent is reviewing. We have a few follow-ups specifically around audit trail portability and retention that we need clarified before we move the security review forward:

1) Exportability: do you support on-demand exports of the full audit event stream per tenant? If so, what formats do you provide (NDJSON, Parquet, compressed tarball)? Are exported timestamps monotonic and RFC3339-compliant?

2) Tamper evidence: can Redwood provide a signed manifest and hash chain for exports (e.g., per-file SHA256 + a signed manifest)?

3) Retention windows: for Dedicated and Private deployments, can retention be set per-tenant and enforced at storage layer? What guarantees exist for immutable retention (legal hold / WORM-like behavior)?

4) Delivery SLA: what's the typical lead time for a bulk export (10TB) and do you provide presigned URLs / S3 push delivery?

5) Proof of continuity: do you provide monotonic event IDs and sequence proof so we can verify no gaps in the delivered export?

If you can reply with short, actionable answers and any example manifests or schema samples we can attach to the security questionnaire, that would be ideal. Please cc Darren (our infra lead) on the reply.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Lowe
Director, Security & Compliance
Candescent Bank
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@candescent.com>
Cc: Darren King <darren.king@candescent.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifications on audit traceability & exportability (RFP CND-9341)

Hannah —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise answers plus I've attached a sample export manifest and a retention mapping CSV. I've cc'd Jonas from Product (audit export schema) so he can jump in if you want schema-level detail.

1) Exportability: Yes — on-demand full audit exports by tenant are supported for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Supported delivery formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), Apache Parquet (columnar), and gzipped tarball (for bundled multi-file deliveries). Timestamps are RFC3339 with timezone offsets and we include both event_time and recorded_time fields. Exports are monotonically ordered by event_time per stream.

2) Tamper evidence: We produce a per-export signed manifest that includes: file list, per-file SHA256, export generation timestamp, total event count, and an incremental export_token. The manifest is signed using our HSM-backed key (RS256). We also optionally generate a chaining file that contains a merkle root over the per-file hashes for additional forensic verification. Attached: export-manifest-sample.json and signed-hash-checksum.txt (signature stub).

3) Retention windows: For Dedicated and Private, retention is configurable at the tenant level via the Redwood Console or API. Policies are enforced by the storage layer: objects are written with immutable retention metadata (S3 Object Lock/Governance or equivalent for on-prem). For Hosted, we offer per-tenant retention tiers; legal holds can be enacted via API to override deletion policies. We provide an audit of retention policy changes (who/when) as part of the tenant audit trail.

4) Delivery SLA: For bulk exports, typical turnaround is: 0–48 hours for <1TB, 48–96 hours for 1–10TB, and 5–10 business days above that depending on size and redaction requirements. Delivery options: presigned S3 URL, direct S3PUT to a customer-bucket (with temporary credentials), or encrypted physical transfer (for extremely large/regulated requests). We include a manifest and checksum on delivery.

5) Proof of continuity: Each audit event includes a monotonic event_id (64-bit numeric) and a sequence_id per shard. Export manifests include first_event_id and last_event_id; we also publish a lightweight continuity proof file with sequence ranges and per-shard checksums so you can detect gaps. We can optionally include a signed snapshot of the highest-seen offset at export time.

Attachments: retention-table-20261207.csv, export-manifest-sample.json, signed-hash-checksum.txt

If Darren wants, we can provide a short runbook showing how to validate the manifest (sha256sum, verify signature, merkle root) and a sample NDJSON export for automated verification.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Darren King <darren.king@candescent.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@candescent.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifications on audit traceability & exportability (RFP CND-9341)

Mina / Jonas —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team before we mark the item as closed:

- Hash verification: are the manifests signed with a customer-verifiable key? We need to be able to verify RS256 signatures against a published certificate or JWKS endpoint (non-interactive).

- Time skew & ordering: you said event_time and recorded_time — in cases where upstream systems have clock skew, how do you guarantee monotonic ordering for export? Do you re-order based on recorded_time or preserve source-provided times and surface reorderings in the manifest?

- Immutable retention proof: can we retrieve a historical policy audit (who set policy X and when) as part of an export package? Ideally the export bundle includes a policy-audit.json that is signed.

Also, for our legal team, do you support a WORM-like SLA (write-once-retain) with attestation for Dedicated and Private installs? If yes, what's the typical certification process to enable it?

Appreciate the detail — Darren
Darren King
Lead, Platform Engineering
Candescent Bank
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Darren King <darren.king@candescent.com>, Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@candescent.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 16:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifications on audit traceability & exportability (RFP CND-9341)

Darren —

Short answers first, then an implementation snippet you can run against a sample export we uploaded to a test S3 link.

- Signature verification: manifests are signed with Redwood's HSM-backed keypair by default, and we publish a JWKS endpoint for verification. For Dedicated/Private customers we can rotate in a customer-provided public key or establish a cross-signed certificate. We include a certificate chain and key id in the manifest header for verification.

- Ordering & skew handling: Redwood preserves source event_time and writes events in ingest order. For export continuity we provide an exported "ordering map" when reordering-induced ambiguities exist — this map lists events that were out-of-order and the canonical ordering used for the export. The manifest includes both event_count and reorder_count.

- Policy audit artifact: yes — export bundles contain policy-audit.json (who/when/policy_id) and it's included in the signed manifest. This file is generated atomically with the export and is covered by the export signature.

- WORM/attestation: For Dedicated and Private we support object immutability using S3 Object Lock (Compliance mode) or equivalent on-prem mechanisms. Enabling requires a one-time configuration change plus a mutually-signed attestation that we provide; we also produce a signed "retention-enablement" artifact showing the retention configuration and enabling timestamp. Certification for WORM is part of our enterprise onboarding with a security gating checklist (we can share the checklist).

Implementation / verification snippet (example flow):
1) Download export bundle (presigned S3 URL provided)
2) Verify manifest signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature manifest.sig export-manifest-sample.json
3) Validate checksums: sha256sum -c export-manifest-sample.json
4) If merkle_root present: verify per-file leaf hashes -> recompute merkle root -> compare to manifest
5) Inspect policy-audit.json and retention metadata files for legal hold flags

We've uploaded a small sample bundle for you to test: https://s3.mock/candescent/export-sample-20261207.ndjson (this link is a short-lived demo presigned URL). The manifest and signature are included in the bundle.

I'll attach the runbook and a short shell script (verify-export.sh) to the final RFP packet if you want. Let me know if you need us to run a handoff demo with your infra team.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
